pr_title: Improve storyboards handling by making use of `TransformSequence.Loop()`
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12401

For storyboards with large loop counts:
* Reduces memory usage
* Speeds up storyboard loading

Examples of maps fixed:
https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/939511
https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/1108479
_Both are unable to run on master_

There was a concern about potential performance issues during rewinding in https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12401#issuecomment-1532630432, however I couldn't recplicate. May be due to a bit different approach or I wasn't looking hard enough.
pr_comments:
So I did a song and dance with generics due to `DrawableStoryboardSprite` and `DrawableStoryboardAnimation` not having a common ancestor, which was a big problem here (this was needed anyway because even with `TransformSequence` approach we will end up splitting stuff per type, which is no longer the case).
In the end looks cleaner I suppose.

issue_context.title: Large loopcounts in storyboard loops may allocate lots of memory
issue_context.body:

**Describe the bug:** 

[Ayane - Nageki no Mori](https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/1108479) is an example of a ranked storyboard that has a loop with a loopcount of 9999999. The sprite itself isn't visible for that long, but the events in the loop stretch out to about 1.9 years. This causes lazer to continue allocating memory for the events until at least my computer crashes.

It gets stuck [over at this function](https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/97879c3c98bcc19012c52e86287b2b8c8f0357ab/osu.Game/Storyboards/CommandLoop.cs#L24), which can be confirmed with a breakpoint. Note that closing osu in this state will leave the thread to continue allocating memory, so watch out for that.

In both diff files:
```
Sprite,Foreground,Centre,"sb\collabpart\_002.png",650,430.75
 L,0,9999999
  R,5,0,3000,-0.01,0.01
  R,5,3000,6000,0.01,-0.01
```

I don't know if stable iterates through the loops differently, but it works fine there. There is no outro on stable because loops don't affect outro time, but in the design editor the invisible sprite can be observed moving way beyond the end of the map. Haven't tested to see if there is any limit, although not sure if a simple limit would be the correct solution.

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 

![Screenshot 2021-04-13 202651](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36758269/114602206-a0b25000-9c96-11eb-9a86-0fa18325446d.png)

**osu!lazer version:** 

Latest release: 2021.410.0

comments: Looping should likely be refactored to only apply the next loop iteration when the previous completes, rather than initialising all loops up-front. If/when this is done, attention should be given to the allocation overhead which will be incurred by the change.

Just as a note, said PR does not fix the issue with any storyboard linked.
Wala's linked storyboard requires at least 15GB of RAM to load fully,
and my storyboard would still require at least 40GB of RAM to load if estimations are still correct due to crashing at 22GB of RAM usage by osu!.
Version: 2023.419.0

The PR linked fixes loops at a framework level. Unfortunately, storyboard command and loop generation is being done locally at the osu! side:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/e330052852a8692c769ed2152a5980a16679b576/osu.Game/Storyboards/StoryboardSprite.cs#L127-L160

![JetBrains Rider 2023-05-03 at 07 48 40](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/235859245-9c539f8e-2515-49c5-9c0e-00bddd47ea4c.png)

I'll take a quick look into whether we can switch this to using framework native loop support.
